reason: E1 and E2 directly support the role of shear-fault energy fluctuations in strength and their persistence, while E5 supports rugged energy landscapes affecting dislocation motion. However, the premise linking high entropy of mixing to more uniform element distribution and higher local fluctuations is not supported by the cited evidence, and E3 actually shows chemical clustering in a high-entropy alloy, contradicting this claim.
premises: Strength in CCAs arises from fluctuations (not average) of shear-fault energy
Local fluctuations in fault energy persist and dominate over elastic misfit contributions
Local chemical fluctuations create hard atomic motifs that pin dislocations
High entropy of mixing leads to more uniform element distribution and higher local chemical fluctuations
